message.content: {"faithfulness":4,"specificity":5,"actionability":2,"clarity":4,"structure":2,"overall":4,"worst_problem":"Every single item's sendLine field is empty, so despite decent research synthesis there is nothing a marketer can actually copy and send — and multiple items pull claims from fieldKeys not in that section's allowedFieldKeys list (e.g. account.abm_program_maturity and account.resonance.buying_culture used in 'how_they_sell'/'tools'; contact.facet.self_summary/headline/alma_mater/stated_skills used in 'contact_insights'), plus a contactRef to Ricardo Lafosse who isn't one of the five tracked contacts.","best_item":"The Nick Fisher contact insight surfacing his own verbatim LinkedIn line — 'we revealed how 96% of vulnerabilities didn't require patching and can be mitigated using existing controls' — is concrete, quotable, and tied directly to a named source."}
message.reasoning:
I'm checking the buying signals claim about excluded platforms against the source record, and I'm counting fourteen named tools in the explicitly-absent list rather than the "10 other platforms" phrasing used.

I'm verifying the field keys and citations used for each buying signal item—hiring velocity, ABM maturity, strategic moves—and they all map to allowed fields correctly. Now I'm cross-checking the funding and momentum section, confirming the recent funding field key is valid and starting to verify the investor names listed against the source.

The claim about lacking ABM/MAP tools checks out fine. But item2's claim about Jira/ServiceNow integration pulls from zaf-140 (account.resonance.buying_culture), which isn't in the allowed field keys for the tools section - that's a genuine structure violation.

Moving to how they sell, item1 references zaf-090 (account.abm_program_maturity), also outside the allowed field list for that section, alongside zaf-140 which is again disallowed here. zaf-127 (core.company_about) is fine, but the other two are clear violations.

For item2, zaf-172 (claimed_customer_logos), zaf-150 (public_frustrations), and zaf-093 (named_customers) all check out against the allowed fields. But I notice the contactRefs list "Ricardo Lafosse," who isn't among the five tracked contacts (Vari Kaur, Nick Fisher, Sanaz Yashar, Ben Seri, Tom Anthony) - he seems to be a customer quote source rather than an actual account contact record, which raises a question about whether this contactRef is valid.

Moving to contact insights, I see one item per person and all five contacts are covered, which matches the instruction correctly. But checking the allowed fieldKeys list for this section against what's actually used reveals problems: Vari Kaur's item pulls in zaf-090 (an account field that shouldn't appear here) plus zaf-029 and zaf-030, neither of which appear on the allowed list at all. There's also a mismatch where the headline claims she won a "CMO Special Mention Award" but the body text never actually substantiates that.

Also the fields used aren't in the allowed key list for this section. Checking Nick Fisher's item next, I see zaf-046 alma_mater cited but that's not an allowed field for this section, only career_history is permitted there. Now looking at Sanaz Yashar's item for similar issues.

Continuing through Sanaz Yashar, Tom Anthony, and Ben Seri entries, I'm spotting the same violation pattern - fields like stated_skills, current_location, and alma_mater keep appearing even though they're outside the allowed field key lists for these sections, while career_history and persona citations are properly compliant. This looks like a systemic issue across the tools, how_they_sell, and contact_insights sections. Now I need to check the context_only section requirements and cross-reference which claims are marked outreachSafe=false to ensure each unsafe fact gets its own item.

I'm now verifying the writer's output covers the unsafe facts - Cisco acquisition rumor, ARR/burn reputation risk, Havdala departure, Nick Fisher's cocktail hobby, Amex Ventures investment, and Sanaz's IDF background all appear covered, but I need to check whether the Cisco strategic investment announcement (zaf-135) is a separate topic from the Cisco rumor (zaf-169) or if they overlap.

Both zaf-135 and zaf-138 overlap in content with claims already covered, so the six distinct facts addressed seem reasonably compliant even though not every claimId got its own explicit mention.

On faithfulness, quotes are mostly verbatim and well-grounded, but there's a minor numeric slip ("10 other platforms" instead of 11) and an uncited claim about the CMO Special Mention Award - I'd rate this around 4. Specificity is strong given the dates, numbers, and quotes used, so that's a 4-5. For actionability, I'm noticing every sendLine field is empty across all items, which matters since the grading criteria specifically checks whether these fields are actually sendable.

Structure also has violations: disallowed fieldKeys used across tools, how_they_sell, and contact_insights sections, plus a contactRef to Ricardo Lafosse who isn't a tracked contact. Combined with the empty sendLine fields everywhere and some missing unsafe facts, this pulls the structure score down too.

Clarity is solid though — the writing is crisp, follows the h2/body/what-it-means format without fluff, so I'll rate that a 4.

Scoring it out: faithfulness 4, specificity 5, actionability 2 (the empty sendLine is a serious gap), clarity 4, structure 2 given the fieldKey and contactRef issues. Overall this lands around 5-6.

The biggest flaw is that sendLine is blank across every item, undermining the whole point of ABM outreach copy. The standout element is the contact_insights item on Nick Fisher, which pulls a concrete, well-sourced verbatim quote from his LinkedIn article about 96% of vulnerabilities not requiring patching — that's the strongest piece of the bunch.
